alison: quick one — ran opsbench against staging to get sane defaults for RPM/TPM + burst window. results attached below, can someone sanity-check before I push to config?

mike: thanks! can you paste the opsbench command you used and sample output?

alison: sure — command:```opsbench --target https://staging-api.redwood.ai --paths '/v1/generate' --concurrency 50 --rate 600 --duration 300 --mix '70:gen,30:embed' --burst-window 10 --api-keys 100``` sample summary: `requests: 1,800,000; 429s: 1.8%; p50: 60ms; p95: 340ms; p99: 1.2s; throughput: 600rpm aggregate; avg tokens/s per req ~ 6`

sandeep: 1.8% 429s is concerning but not huge — were 429s concentrated on a small subset of keys?

alison: yes, heatmap shows top 10 keys saw >5% 429s, rest <0.5%. looks like fairshare kicking in + burst exhaustion for hot keys.

jules: do we see any backend GPU saturation or queueing at the runtime level at those times? logs?

alison: runtime traces show CPU at 65% per node, GPU utilization steady ~72%, but connection queue length spiked for a few seconds when burst started. attached log snippet:```[12:02:11] conn_queue=49 latency_headroom=120ms fairshare_dropped=12```

lee: that suggests policy-level throttles rather than hardware OOM. If fairshare is dropping 12 concurrent requests, it's likely our per-key burst tokens exhausted. What did you set per-key default?

alison: current per-key default in config is RPM=100, TPM=3000 with burst multiplier 3 for a 30s window. I was proposing to reduce base RPM to 80 and keep burst multiplier 2 for 10s window (so short spikes allowed but not long sustained surges).

mike: any regressions on latency after lowering RPM in the lab?

alison: when I re-ran with per-key RPM=80 and burst-window=10 + burst-mult=2 (i.e., short burst cap), aggregate 429s dropped to 0.4%, p95 improved to 310ms, p99 to 980ms. error rates moved from hot keys to a small % of keys only during sustained long bursts.

sandeep: good. sounds conservative and reduces noisy neighbor impact. Two quick asks: (1) can we reproduce with mixed key sizes (1k req/day vs 1M req/day) to validate fairness heuristics? (2) run a long tail test 1hr with exponential burst shape to check policy bleed-over.

alison: yes — plan: run two tests tomorrow: small-key-heavy (95% small keys) and longtail (Pareto 80/20). I'll add `--key-profile small:10000,large:50` and `--burst-shape pareto --duration 3600`.

jules: add a test where we do token-heavy generation (long seq) vs short chat-like calls — quantization affects tokens/s and changes TPM behaviour.

alison: will do. also noted billing delta: during initial runs some customers saw unexpected invoice spikes because our billing window aggregates token rounding differently when we drop requests. ops-bot flagged 4 tickets.

ops-bot: [alert] 4 billing tickets created for staging keys during opsbench run — reference #BILL-3142.

lee: for billing we should ensure dropped requests aren't billed; add explicit check to the billing pipeline to ignore 4xx/429. If not possible, document the billing implications for enterprise customers.

mike: next steps: alison to run the two follow-up tests + token-heavy run, collect per-key histograms (p50/p95/p99) and heatmaps, then propose final defaults to staging-config PR. If all good we'll roll to canary with monitoring thresholds.

alison: on it. ETA next day. will dump opsbench commands + artifacts in the bench-drive and ping here. :thumbsup:

lee: thanks — also include a short reproducible playbook for support: steps to repro, commands, what logs to attach, and suggested communication template for customers hit by temporary throttles.

alison: will add playbook. sample repro snippet I'll include:```# reproduce hot-key 429s
for i in {1..1000}; do curl -s -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $HOT_KEY" -d '{"prompt":"ok","max_tokens":16}' & done; wait
```

mike: perfect. low-effort and easy to run in any sandbox. thanks team.
